analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. The visible hunks are a date bump (line 3) and edits to the GLM5Next reasoning-control table (about lines 1147-1153). Those changed ranges lie outside the two supplied units, which show only head-side lines 326-582 and 583-954. The supplied text is unchanged surrounding documentation: PrefixCacheV2 capability fields, donation outcomes, heartbeat, backend_capacity, telemetry, models_replace, and the inference and attestation messages.

I reviewed the surrounding text against the threat model, mainly TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041, T-053 and T-056. It makes no new security claims. It states that the telemetry objects (prefix_cache, paged_storage, process_memory) are diagnostic only and do not affect routing, admission or authorization. It also says the coordinator never reads provider-authored inference_error text, and it requires a code_attestation_response signature to verify against the key bound at registration. These are consistent with existing assumptions, and no controls are weakened.

Prefix-cache wording (checkpoint ready_boundary_mode, donation outcomes) does not change the at-rest or TTL posture described in T-041. Doc links are pinned to immutable platform commits, so they carry no code or deployment change.

The only substantive change visible in the patch is the GLM5Next reasoning-control documentation. It says null reasoning is unset, summary and generate_summary are no-ops, and other members are refused. That is request-parsing documentation and has no visible security effect. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the reasoning-table edits (lines 1149-1153) were not visible and are unreviewed. Whether the provider source matches the documented refusal behavior is an unverified contract, but it is not evidence of a regression. No findings.
